newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Government has unveiled a string of measures aimed at opening new revenue streams for the ailing Post Office while delivering up to 500 000 new postal addresses to disadvantaged communities each year.

- New information had forced the reopening of the investigation into the cause of the 1987 crash of SA Airways' Helderberg aircraft, which killed all 159 passengers and crew, sources said on Thursday.
- Gold fields of SA, the country's second largest gold producer, aims to increase gold production by 46.8 tons over the next year as part of boosting gold production 90 tons.
- The Cancer Association of SA had withdrawn an anti-smoking radio advertisement after threats of legal action by Riggio Tobacco Corporation of New York, spokesman Katherine Everett said on Thursday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- ERPM, the troubled mine in the Randgold stable and once one of the largest and most profitable gold mines in the world, is on the point of closure, a victim of the low gold price, the company said on Thursday.

- Anglogold, the world's largest gold producer, and a division of Anglo American, saw profit fall only 2 percent this quarter, in spite of the depressed international bullion price the company said on Thursday..
- South Africa has a bad mane when it comes to insider trading, Russell Loubser, the JSE president, said on Thursday.

- The government was considering a partial privatisation of Postbank, which uses the Post Office network to provide banking facilities to traditionally "unbankable" rural communities, Jay Naidoo, the minister of posts and telecommunications, said on Thursday.

- The South African Clothing and Textile Workers' Union warned on Thursday it would not hesitate to act against South African companies involved in the mass dismissal of 13 000 Ximbabwean clothing workers this week.
SAKE BEELD
- There is a strong possibility that East Rand Proprietary Mines (ERPM), one of the important employer in the mining trade, will in the near future close its industry.
- The government is going to appoint a task group on corruption in the state service.
THE STAR
- Johannesburg's top 10 traffic offenders owe more than 37,000 rand in unpaid fines, with the number one transgressor liable for a whopping 12 360 rand.
- The discovery of five more bodies in Phoenix, KwaZulu-Natal, brought to 18 the number of women believed to have been murdered by a serial killer stalking the area.

- Police commissioner George Fivaz said on Thursday "significant progress" had been made in tracking down the killers of five ANC members massacred at Richmond, KwaZulu-Natal, after a local by-election there this week.
